def-sample-covariance-empirical-spectral:
## Definition

For positive integers $n$ and $p$, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ and define its (uncentered, unit-variance-normalized) sample covariance matrix by
$$S(X):=\frac1nX^{\mathsf T}X\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}.$$
It is real symmetric and non-negative. If its eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, are $\lambda_1(S(X)),\ldots,\lambda_p(S(X))$, its empirical spectral distribution (ESD), normalized by the matrix dimension $p$, is
$$\mu_{S(X)}:=\frac1p\sum_{j=1}^p\delta_{\lambda_j(S(X))}.$$
The largest eigenvalue is $\lambda_{\max}(S(X)):=\max_j\lambda_j(S(X))$. When $S(X)$ has at least one positive eigenvalue, its smallest positive eigenvalue is $\lambda_{\min}^{+}(S(X)):=\min\{\lambda_j(S(X)):\lambda_j(S(X))>0\}$. For a sequence $X_n\in\mathbb R^{n\times p_n}$, write $S_n=S(X_n)$ and $\mu_n=\mu_{S_n}$.
def-stieltjes-transform-of-a-real-probab:
## Definition

Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$. For $z=u+i\eta$ with $u\in\mathbb R$ and $\eta>0$, its Stieltjes transform, with the $(x-z)^{-1}$ convention, is
$$m_\mu(z):=\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{1}{x-z}\,d\mu(x).$$
The integral is finite because $|x-z|^{-1}\le\eta^{-1}$ for every real $x$.
def-marchenko-pastur-measure:
## Definition

For $\gamma>0$, set
$$a_\gamma=(1-\sqrt\gamma)^2,\qquad b_\gamma=(1+\sqrt\gamma)^2,\qquad r_+:=\max\{r,0\}\quad(r\in\mathbb R).$$
Define the Marchenko–Pastur set function on Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb R$ by
$$\mu_\gamma(A):=\int_{A\cap(a_\gamma,b_\gamma)}\frac{\sqrt{(b_\gamma-x)(x-a_\gamma)}}{2\pi\gamma x}\,d\lambda(x)+\left(1-\frac1\gamma\right)_+\delta_0(A),$$
where $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R$. The formula defines a finite Borel measure; its total mass is established by the Marchenko–Pastur law below.
lem-fourth-moment-quadratic-form-resolve:
## Statement

Let $\xi=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d)^{\mathsf T}$ have independent identically distributed real coordinates with $\mathbb E\xi_i=0$, $\mathbb E\xi_i^2=1$, and $\mu_4:=\mathbb E\xi_i^4<\infty$. Let $A$ be an independent random complex symmetric $d\times d$ matrix with $\mathbb E\|A\|_F^2<\infty$, where $\|A\|_F^2:=\sum_{i,j}|A_{ij}|^2$. Then
$$\mathbb E\left|\xi^{\mathsf T}A\xi-\operatorname{tr}A\right|^2\le C_{\mu_4}\,\mathbb E\|A\|_F^2,\qquad C_{\mu_4}:=\max\{\mu_4-1,2\}.$$
lem-rank-one-resolvent-update-and-trace-:
## Statement

Let $B$ be a real symmetric non-negative $d\times d$ matrix, let $x\in\mathbb R^d$, and let $z=u+i\eta$ with $u\in\mathbb R$ and $\eta>0$. Put $R=(B-zI)^{-1}$ and $R_x=(B+xx^{\mathsf T}-zI)^{-1}$. Then $1+x^{\mathsf T}Rx\ne0$,
$$R_x=R-\frac{Rxx^{\mathsf T}R}{1+x^{\mathsf T}Rx},$$
and
$$\left|\operatorname{tr}R_x-\operatorname{tr}R\right|\le\frac1\eta.$$
lem-uniform-row-partial-sums-of-nested-f:
## Statement

Let $(Z_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be one infinite iid real array with $EZ_{11}=0$ and $EZ_{11}^2<\infty$. For every fixed $C<\infty$,
$$\frac1n\max_{1\le i\le\lfloor Cn\rfloor}\max_{1\le k\le n}\left|\sum_{j=1}^{k}Z_{ij}\right|\longrightarrow0\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
The maximum over an empty index set is zero. The same conclusion holds with row and column coordinates exchanged.
lem-fixed-degree-covariance-trace-and-ed:
## Statement

Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be one infinite real iid array with $E\xi_{11}=0$, $E\xi_{11}^2=1$ and $E|\xi_{11}|^2<\infty$. Let $p_n/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, $X_n=(\xi_{ij})_{i\le n,j\le p_n}$ and $G_n=X_nX_n^{\mathsf T}/n$. Suppose almost surely $\limsup_n\|X_n/\sqrt n\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$. For every fixed integer $k\ge1$, almost surely
$$\frac1n\operatorname{Tr}G_n^k\longrightarrow\mu_k(\gamma):=\sum_{s=1}^k\frac1k\binom{k}{s}\binom{k}{s-1}\gamma^s.$$
Positive eigenvalues exist eventually and, with $a=(1-\sqrt\gamma)^2$ and $b=(1+\sqrt\gamma)^2$, almost surely
$$\liminf_n\lambda_{\max}(G_n)\ge b,\qquad\limsup_n\lambda_{\min}^{+}(G_n)\le a.$$
The edge conclusions follow from fixed polynomial trace witnesses and do not assume a weak empirical spectral limit.
lem-sample-covariance-empirical-law-is-a:
## Statement

For positive integers $n,p$ and a real matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, set $S(X)=X^{\mathsf T}X/n$ and $\mu_{S(X)}=p^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^p\delta_{\lambda_j(S(X))}$, where the eigenvalues are counted with multiplicity. Then $\mu_{S(X)}$ is a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$, supported on $[0,\infty)$.
lem-adapted-resolvent-trace-concentratio:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For each positive integer $n$, let $Y_{n,1},\ldots,Y_{n,n}$ be independent random vectors in $\mathbb R^{d_n}$, let $B_n=\sum_{j=1}^{n}Y_{n,j}Y_{n,j}^{\mathsf T}$, and let $z=u+i\eta$ with fixed $u\in\mathbb R$ and $\eta>0$. Define
$$M_n(z):=\frac1{d_n}\operatorname{tr}(B_n-zI)^{-1}.$$
If $d_n/n\to c$ for some $c\in(0,\infty)$, then $M_n(z)-\mathbb E[M_n(z)]\to0$ almost surely. More precisely, for every $t>0$,
$$\Pr\left\{|M_n(z)-\mathbb E M_n(z)|>t\right\} \le4\exp\left(-\frac{t^2d_n^2\eta^2}{4n}\right).$$
lem-marchenko-pastur-formula-defines-a-f:
## Statement

For every $\gamma>0$, the set function $\mu_\gamma$ in the definition of the Marchenko–Pastur measure is a Borel probability measure supported on $[0,\infty)$. For every $z\in\mathbb C$ with $\eta:=\operatorname{Im}z>0$, its Stieltjes transform $m_\gamma(z)$ satisfies
$$1+z m_\gamma(z)=\frac{m_\gamma(z)}{1+\gamma m_\gamma(z)},\qquad \operatorname{Im}\bigl(1-\gamma-z-\gamma z m_\gamma(z)\bigr)\le-\eta.$$
lem-stieltjes-transform-inversion-and-un:
## Statement

Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$, with Stieltjes transform $m_\mu(z)=\int (x-z)^{-1}\,d\mu(x)$ for $\operatorname{Im}z>0$. For every $a<b$ and $x\in\mathbb R$,
$$\mu((a,b))+\tfrac12\mu(\{a\})+\tfrac12\mu(\{b\})=\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\frac1\pi\int_a^b\operatorname{Im}m_\mu(u+i\eta)\,du,\qquad \mu(\{x\})=\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\eta\,\operatorname{Im}m_\mu(x+i\eta).$$
If two Borel probability measures on $\mathbb R$ have the same Stieltjes transform on the upper half-plane, then they are equal.
lem-nested-iid-fourth-moment-truncation-:
## Statement

Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be one infinite iid real array with $E\xi_{11}=0$, $E\xi_{11}^2=1$ and $E|\xi_{11}|^4<\infty$. Consider any deterministic rectangular sequence $R_n\times C_n$ with both $R_n/n$ and $C_n/n$ bounded above and bounded away from zero. Write $X_n=(\xi_{ij})_{i\le R_n,j\le C_n}$ and $N_n=\max(R_n,C_n)$. There is a deterministic sequence $\delta_n\to0$, which may be chosen to decrease more slowly than any specified finite list of rates tending to zero and to satisfy $\delta_n\ge1/\log(n+2)$, such that, almost surely, $X_n$ equals its entrywise truncation at $\delta_n\sqrt{N_n}$ eventually. Set
$$\widehat\xi_{ij}^{(n)}=\xi_{ij}\mathbf1_{\{|\xi_{ij}|\le\delta_n\sqrt{N_n}\}},\quad\mu_n=E\widehat\xi_{11}^{(n)},\quad x_{ij}^{(n)}=\widehat\xi_{ij}^{(n)}-\mu_n.$$
Then $\sqrt{R_nC_n/N_n}|\mu_n|\to0$, $E|x_{11}^{(n)}|^2\le1$ tends to $1$, $|x_{ij}^{(n)}|\le2\delta_n\sqrt{N_n}$ eventually, and $E|x_{11}^{(n)}|^q\le K(2\delta_n\sqrt{N_n})^{q-3}$ for every integer $q\ge3$, with $K$ independent of $n,q$. Almost surely the following controls hold for the original entries and for the centered truncated entries:
$$\max_{i\le R_n}\left|N_n^{-1}\sum_{j\le C_n}|x_{ij}^{(n)}|^2-C_n/N_n\right|\to0,\qquad\max_{j\le C_n}\left|N_n^{-1}\sum_{i\le R_n}|x_{ij}^{(n)}|^2-R_n/N_n\right|\to0,$$
$$\max_{i\le R_n,j\le C_n}|x_{ij}^{(n)}|/\sqrt{N_n}\to0,\qquad N_n^{-2}\sum_{i\le R_n,j\le C_n}|x_{ij}^{(n)}|^4=O(1).$$
For every fixed $q>2$, the rectangular matrix with entry $N_n^{-q/2}|x_{ij}^{(n)}|^q$ has Frobenius norm tending to zero; the assertion also holds with a sign attached to each entry.
thm-marchenko-pastur-law-for-sample-cova:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For each positive integer $n$, let $p_n$ be a positive integer with $p_n/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, and let $X_n\in\mathbb R^{n\times p_n}$ have mutually independent entries with one common law, mean zero, variance one, and finite fourth moment. Set $S_n=X_n^{\mathsf T}X_n/n$ and let $\mu_n$ be its empirical spectral distribution normalized by $p_n$. Then $\mu_n$ converges weakly almost surely to the probability measure with density
$$\rho_\gamma(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\sqrt{(b_\gamma-x)(x-a_\gamma)}}{2\pi\gamma x},&a_\gamma<x<b_\gamma,\\0,&x\notin(a_\gamma,b_\gamma),\end{cases}\qquad a_\gamma=(1-\sqrt\gamma)^2,\quad b_\gamma=(1+\sqrt\gamma)^2,$$
and an atom of mass $(1-1/\gamma)_+$ at zero.
lem-nonbacktracking-covariance-high-mome:
## Statement

Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be one infinite real iid array with $E\xi_{11}=0$, $E\xi_{11}^2=1$ and $E|\xi_{11}|^4<\infty$, and let $p_h/h\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$. Put $N_h=\max(h,p_h)$, $m_h=\min(h,p_h)$ and $y_h=m_h/N_h\to y:=\min(\gamma,\gamma^{-1})$. Take the centered slow truncations of the upper-left $h\times p_h$ blocks, orient each with $m_h$ rows and $N_h$ columns, and divide by $\sqrt{N_h}$, obtaining $Y_h$. For each fixed integer $\ell\ge1$, define $T_{h,\ell}$ by summing the products of the entries of $Y_h,Y_h^{\mathsf T},\ldots,Y_h,Y_h^{\mathsf T}$ along all paths of length $2\ell$, subject to every pair of vertices two positions apart being unequal. Its row and column endpoints are included in these exclusions. Then almost surely
$$\limsup_h\|T_{h,\ell}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le(2\ell+1)(\ell+1)y^{(\ell-1)/2}.$$
In particular, for the original untruncated $X_h=(\xi_{ij})_{i\le h,j\le p_h}$, almost surely $\limsup_h\|X_h/\sqrt h\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$.
lem-largest-sample-covariance-eigenvalue:
## Statement

Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be one infinite iid array of real random variables with mean zero, variance one and finite fourth moment. For each $n$, let $X_n=(\xi_{ij})_{1\le i\le n,1\le j\le p_n}$ and suppose $p_n/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$. For $S_n=X_n^{\mathsf T}X_n/n$ and $b_\gamma=(1+\sqrt\gamma)^2$, the separate lower-edge estimate is
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\lambda_{\max}(S_n)\ge b_\gamma\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
lem-sample-covariance-spectrum-confineme:
## Statement

Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be one infinite real iid array with $E\xi_{11}=0$, $E\xi_{11}^2=1$ and $E|\xi_{11}|^4<\infty$. Let $X_h=(\xi_{ij})_{i\le h,j\le p_h}$ with $p_h/h\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, $N_h=\max(h,p_h)$ and $m_h=\min(h,p_h)$. Orient $X_h$ or its transpose as a matrix $Z_h$ with $m_h$ rows and $N_h$ columns, and put $A_h=Z_h/\sqrt{N_h}$ and $y=\min(\gamma,\gamma^{-1})\in(0,1]$. Then almost surely
$$\limsup_h\left\|A_hA_h^{\mathsf T}-(1+y)I_{m_h}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\sqrt y.$$
No weak convergence of empirical spectral measures is assumed.
lem-largest-sample-covariance-eigenvalue:
## Statement

Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be one infinite iid array of real random variables with mean zero, variance one and finite fourth moment. For each $n$, let $X_n=(\xi_{ij})_{1\le i\le n,1\le j\le p_n}$ and suppose $p_n/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$. For $S_n=X_n^{\mathsf T}X_n/n$, with $b_\gamma=(1+\sqrt\gamma)^2$, the upper-edge bound is
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\lambda_{\max}(S_n)\le b_\gamma\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
thm-bai-yin-smallest-singular-value-limi:
## Statement

Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be one infinite iid array of real random variables with mean zero, variance one and finite fourth moment. For each $n$, let $X_n=(\xi_{ij})_{1\le i\le n,1\le j\le p_n}$ and suppose $p_n/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$. Let $s_{r_n}(X_n)$ be the smallest among the $r_n:=\min(n,p_n)$ singular values, counting zero values. Then, almost surely: if $\gamma<1$, $s_{r_n}(X_n)/\sqrt n\to1-\sqrt\gamma$, so $X_n$ has full column rank for all sufficiently large $n$; if $\gamma>1$, $s_{r_n}(X_n)/\sqrt n\to\sqrt\gamma-1$, so $X_n$ has full row rank for all sufficiently large $n$; and if $\gamma=1$, the smallest positive singular value is eventually defined and, divided by $\sqrt n$, tends to zero.
thm-largest-eigenvalue-sample-covariance:
## Statement

Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be one infinite iid array of real random variables with mean zero, variance one and finite fourth moment. For each $n$, let $X_n=(\xi_{ij})_{1\le i\le n,1\le j\le p_n}$ and suppose $p_n/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$. For $S_n=X_n^{\mathsf T}X_n/n$, the largest eigenvalue satisfies
$$\lambda_{\max}(S_n)\longrightarrow(1+\sqrt\gamma)^2\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
thm-smallest-positive-eigenvalue-sample-:
## Statement

Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be one infinite iid array of real random variables with mean zero, variance one and finite fourth moment. For each $n$, let $X_n=(\xi_{ij})_{1\le i\le n,1\le j\le p_n}$ and suppose $p_n/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$. Set $S_n=X_n^{\mathsf T}X_n/n$ and let $\lambda_{\min}^{+}(S_n)$ denote its smallest positive eigenvalue whenever one exists. If $\gamma<1$, then almost surely $X_n$ has full column rank for all sufficiently large $n$, so $S_n$ has no zero eigenvalues eventually and $\lambda_{\min}(S_n)\to(1-\sqrt\gamma)^2$. If $\gamma>1$, then almost surely $X_n$ has full row rank for all sufficiently large $n$, so $S_n$ has exactly $p_n-n$ zero eigenvalues and $\lambda_{\min}^{+}(S_n)\to(\sqrt\gamma-1)^2$. If $\gamma=1$, then almost surely $\lambda_{\min}^{+}(S_n)\to0$.
